_comment: Single source of truth for the numeric thresholds that gate decision surfaces. src/api/thresholds.py LOADS this file, so the Python side cannot drift from it. frontend/lib/thresholds.js mirrors it statically and tests/api/test_threshold_parity.py enforces the match - the same mirror+parity mechanism as the ranking-source registry, which is the one that demonstrably works in this repo. Every entry records how its value was derived; an entry without a derivation is a number someone invented.

MARKET_GAP_MIN_MAGNITUDE.derivedFrom: p50 of |de-meaned market gap| across the 414 rows carrying one on the 2026-08-05 board (25.8). Replaces MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF=10, which was 10 ORDINAL RANKS - about 21 per-mille on the 469-deep retail board, so this floor sits within 20% of the old one while being expressed in a unit that means the same thing on every source.

MARKET_PREMIUM_MAGNITUDE.derivedFrom: p70 of the same distribution (51.8) - the cut above which a gap is worth an action label rather than a note. Replaces MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD=30 ranks (~64 per-mille), so slightly more inclusive, chosen on a measured landmark rather than the old round number.

PREMIUM_SUMMARY_MAGNITUDE.derivedFrom: Same p70 cut; yields 127 candidate rows before the top-250 filter and the 10-row slice. The gate it replaces for these panels (PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD>=20) admitted 376 of 414 rows - 91%, effectively inert - AND measured source disagreement rather than the gap whose sign the panel displays.

MIN_EDGE_MAGNITUDE.derivedFrom: Deliberately equal to MARKET_GAP_MIN_MAGNITUDE: if the board will not label a gap, a trade surface must not signal on it. Replaces MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP=3 ranks (~6 per-mille), which admitted essentially every row and was therefore never a decision - porting it forward would have preserved a non-choice as if it were one.

MARKET_GAP_MIN_POSITION_N.derivedFrom: Floor below which a position's median gap is noise rather than a basis. Every position on the live board clears it comfortably (WR 146, RB 103, TE 72, QB 57, PICK 36), so it binds only on a coverage collapse - which is exactly when de-meaning off a tiny sample would invent a constant out of the noise it exists to remove.

PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD.derivedFrom: Pre-existing. RETAINED but NARROWED: it now gates only the /edge disagreements panel and the disagreement stat, which are genuinely about sources disagreeing with each other. The premium panels moved to PREMIUM_SUMMARY_MAGNITUDE.

MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD.derivedFrom: Pre-existing spread gate, unchanged. Distinct from MARKET_PREMIUM_MAGNITUDE despite the similar name - this one is about disagreement width, that one about the retail-vs-consensus gap.

LENS_INEFFICIENCY_RANK.derivedFrom: Pre-existing rankings-page lens eligibility cap. Unchanged.

EDGE_CAUTION_RANK_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Pre-existing /edge cap for flagged and single-source sections. Unchanged.

EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Pre-existing. Raised 150 -> 250 on 2026-04-29 to surface mid-board WR/RB disagreements; see the note in frontend/lib/thresholds.js. Unchanged by this batch.

RANKINGS_DEFAULT_ROW_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Page-level UX choice, not a data threshold: how many rows /rankings paints before 'show more'. Listed here so this file is the COMPLETE inventory of the frontend's numeric constants - the parity test allows no exemptions, because an exemption list is where an unreviewed threshold would hide.

FINDER_ROW_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Page-level UX choice: maximum rows per workflow on /finder. Not a data threshold.

EDGE_SECTION_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Page-level UX choice: items per /edge section. Not a data threshold.

EDGE_PREMIUM_LIMIT.derivedFrom: Page-level UX choice: items per /edge premium panel, applied AFTER the magnitude gate and the top-250 filter. Not a data threshold.

MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF.derivedFrom: Pre-existing, and DELIBERATELY still in ordinal ranks. It gates only frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::idpMarketEdge, the one surviving client-side gap computation. That path exists because the backend emits NO market gap for IDP at all - the sole is_retail source publishes no defenders, so all 386 IDP rows abstain with reason 'consensus_only' - and deleting it would remove a working surface to satisfy a rule. It carries audit finding S-1 (raw ordinals across boards of different depth) exactly as the offense path did before C4. Tracked as the IDP-anchor follow-up: give the backend an IDP retail anchor, stamp the gap, then delete this and its threshold together.

_removed.CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH / CONFIDENCE_SPRE: Removed 2026-08-05 by #725, and this file follows rather than resurrecting them. They claimed to mirror the backend's confidence buckets and did not: _confidence_bucket decides off the PERCENTILE spread on the live path, and their one consumer re-applied the retired ordinal rule on top of the backend's verdict, suppressing 'Consensus asset' on 54 of 111 qualifying rows. A threshold with no reader does not belong in an inventory of live thresholds - and listing one here would make test_threshold_parity.py demand the JS export it back.
